items.headline: 52 Singaporeans are detained in China over a suspected pyramid scheme
items.summary: Singapore's MFA said on Sep 4 that 52 Singaporeans have been arrested and detained in Guangxi, China, over suspected pyramid-scheme offences; consular visits were made to all 52.

items.headline: Four arrested over 'phantom worker' CPF fraud used to inflate foreign-worker quotas
items.summary: MOM arrested four people from the construction sector in a Sep 2 operation; two directors allegedly made fraudulent CPF contributions for locals not in their employ to inflate foreign-worker quotas.

items.headline: Singaporean man, 40, arrested in Bangkok over dark-web drug and poison orders
items.summary: A 40-year-old Singaporean was arrested in Bangkok on Sep 4 with drug paraphernalia and poisonous substances, plus evidence he had ordered such materials on the dark web.

items.headline: British man, 25, jailed after a drunken Changi Airport ruckus triggers an anti-hijack alert
items.summary: A 25-year-old British man was jailed and fined after a drunken disturbance at Changi Airport prompted security to press an anti-hijack button.

items.headline: A former finance secretary alleges India's 7.8% GDP print was flattered by revisions
items.summary: Ex-finance secretary Subhash Chandra Garg alleged the April-June GDP reading was boosted by compressing the prior year's base, a charge echoed by the Congress; Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said 'India's 7.8% growth is a reality'.

items.headline: The RBI drains cash for longer as a liquidity surge tests its policy grip
items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India held a 7 trillion rupee (about US$74 billion) 30-day variable-rate reverse repo auction on Sep 4, shifting to longer drains to absorb surplus liquidity after record inflows.

items.headline: India's 'Cockroach' group calls off its Sept 5 Delhi march after the top court drops cases
items.summary: The Cockroach Janta Party shelved its planned Sep 5 New Delhi march after a Supreme Court bench led by CJI Surya Kant ordered criminal cases dropped against July's student protesters and barred fresh cases.

items.headline: Update: Xi Jinping is expected in New Delhi for his first India visit in seven years
items.summary: China's Xi Jinping is expected in New Delhi in the coming days for his first India visit in seven years, moving beyond last week's eight border-easing steps; the Himalayan border, trade and visas top the agenda.

items.headline: PM Andy Burnham faces his first Commons grilling, vowing to 'bring back hope'
items.summary: In his first Commons appearance as PM, Andy Burnham fielded questions on the economy and immigration and pledged to 'bring back hope' as MPs returned from recess.

items.headline: Chancellor Healey is urged to rebuild the UK's fiscal buffer before the October budget
items.summary: Bloomberg Economics said Chancellor John Healey should restore most of the fiscal headroom eroded by a global bond sell-off at his Oct 28 budget to reassure investors.

items.headline: Burnham commits to the fiscal rules but declines to rule out more borrowing
items.summary: PM Andy Burnham said his government would keep to its fiscal rules and deliver stability, but declined to rule out additional borrowing, signalling he may use flexibility within the rules in the autumn budget.

items.headline: 'Stop the boats' protesters in masks block England's Port of Dover
items.summary: Masked demonstrators protesting small-boat migrant crossings blocked access to the Port of Dover, disrupting one of England's busiest Channel crossings as immigration stays a flashpoint.

items.headline: The US says it struck Iranian oil tankers it accuses of financing regional proxies
items.summary: US forces said they hit Iranian oil tankers alleged to help finance Tehran's regional proxies, the latest escalation in a conflict now in its seventh month, renewing fears for Gulf shipping.

items.headline: A Philippine court orders the arrest of Vice-President Sara Duterte over threats to Marcos
items.summary: A Philippine court ordered the arrest of Vice-President Sara Duterte over threats she made against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr, a sharp escalation in the feud between the two political dynasties.

items.headline: Trump says Witkoff and Kushner will travel to 'end' Russia's war in Ukraine
items.summary: President Donald Trump said envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner would travel abroad in a fresh push to 'end' Russia's war in Ukraine, as Kyiv warned that delays in Western support were emboldening Moscow.

items.headline: The UN backs a new world map that shows Africa's true size
items.summary: The UN endorsed a shift toward an equal-area world map that renders Africa at its true scale, backing a 'Correct the Map' campaign arguing the Mercator projection has long shrunk the continent.

items.headline: Two pilots are killed as a Greek fighter jet crashes at an air show
items.summary: Two pilots were killed when a Greek air force fighter jet crashed during an air-show display, Greek authorities said, opening an investigation into the cause.

items.headline: Apple sets a Sept 9 event to launch its first foldable iPhone under CEO John Ternus
items.summary: Apple's biggest launch of the year, on Sep 9 and the first under new CEO John Ternus, is expected to unveil its foldable iPhone alongside the iPhone 18 Pro, new Apple Watches and a wider Siri rollout.

items.headline: US regulators open a probe into Tesla's Cybercab hours after its Austin launch
items.summary: The NHTSA opened an investigation into Tesla's Cybercab within hours of the first vehicles reaching Austin streets on Sep 4, questioning its lack of a steering wheel or pedals under federal safety rules.

items.headline: Meta releases its Muse Spark model with a steep discount for users who share prompts
items.summary: Meta released Muse Spark, its most capable AI model yet for coding and agent tasks, paired with pricing offering roughly a 95% discount to users who let Meta study their prompts and outputs to train future models.

items.headline: Palo Alto Networks buys IT-automation startup Console for about US$500 million
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks paid around US$500 million in cash and stock for Console, a two-year-old startup whose AI agents automate IT help-desk tasks; Console had raised US$29 million from backers including Thrive Capital and DST Global.

items.headline: US payrolls jump 162,000 in August as the jobless rate holds at 4.1%
items.summary: US employers added 162,000 jobs in August, far above the roughly 53,000 expected and the strongest since March, while unemployment held at 4.1%. Bars and restaurants led hiring; information-sector jobs fell.

items.headline: The 2-year Treasury yield hits its highest since January 2025 after the hot jobs report
items.summary: The 2-year Treasury yield rose to its highest since January 2025 after the strong jobs report, as traders lifted odds of a Fed hike at the Sep 15-16 meeting to about 60%; the Dow fell more than 260 points.

items.headline: Tesla shares slide more than 6% after the Cybercab's rocky debut
items.summary: Tesla shares fell more than 6% on Sep 4, on pace for their worst day since late July, after the Cybercab launch in Austin was quickly met with a federal safety probe.

items.headline: Lululemon shares plunge about 20% on a weak outlook
items.summary: Lululemon shares tumbled about 20% in premarket trading on Sep 4 after a disappointing outlook, with the athletic-apparel maker guiding to third-quarter earnings of about 93 to 98 cents a share.

items.headline: Gasly stuns Monza with a maiden pole for the Italian Grand Prix
items.summary: Alpine's Pierre Gasly took the first pole of his F1 career, clocking 1:21.786 to edge George Russell by 0.060s at Monza, with Oscar Piastri third and Ferraris Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton fourth and fifth.

items.headline: Championship leader Antonelli will start at the back at Monza after an engine penalty
items.summary: Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli, who leads the drivers' standings, qualified seventh but will drop to the back of the Italian Grand Prix grid after taking a new power unit.

items.headline: India bowl Pakistan out for 55 and win by seven wickets at the Women's Asia Cup
items.summary: India routed Pakistan by seven wickets in Dubai, bowling them out for 55 (reportedly Pakistan's lowest women's T20I total), with Shree Charani 3-7 and Prema Rawat 3-9, then chasing down the target for the loss of three wickets.

items.headline: Sabalenka and Pegula reach the US Open fourth round
items.summary: Top seed Aryna Sabalenka advanced in straight sets while No. 3 Jessica Pegula fought back to beat Leylah Fernandez 1-6, 6-4, 6-3 to set up a fourth-round tie with Sorana Cirstea.

items.headline: Alcaraz beats Wu Yibing to set up a US Open last-16 tie with Tommy Paul
items.summary: Second seed Carlos Alcaraz beat Wu Yibing 6-3, 6-4, 6-1 to reach the US Open fourth round, where he will face American Tommy Paul.

items.headline: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope launches to map dark energy and hunt planets
items.summary: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope launched Aug 30 on a SpaceX Falcon Heavy from Kennedy Space Center. With a field of view about 100 times Hubble's, it will probe dark energy and image exoplanets; its coronagraph powered on Sep 1.

items.headline: Webb finds a giant black hole that seems to have formed before its galaxy
items.summary: JWST observations of QSO1, seen about 700 million years after the Big Bang, suggest a supermassive black hole of roughly 40 million solar masses that appears to have grown before a full host galaxy formed around it.

items.headline: A new chicken-sized dinosaur from Spain puzzles palaeontologists
items.summary: Researchers describing Foskeia pelendonum, a plant-eating dinosaur about half a metre long that lived in northern Spain some 125 million years ago, say its unusual skull and teeth point to a 'novel mode of feeding'; the find appeared in Papers in Palaeontology.

items.headline: A new report warns the world will blow past the 1.5C limit within a few years
items.summary: A report published Sep 2 concludes that global warming is on track to breach the Paris Agreement's 1.5C threshold within the next few years on current emissions trends.

fun_fact.headline: The Sun is 99.8% of the solar system's mass
fun_fact.body: The Sun accounts for about 99.8% of all the mass in the solar system. Everything else - the eight planets, their moons, and every asteroid and comet combined - makes up less than a fifth of one percent. That overwhelming mass anchors the Sun's gravity, holding worlds in orbit from tiny Mercury out to the distant Oort Cloud.

puzzle.title: Crossing in the Dark
puzzle.body: Four hikers must cross a rickety bridge at night with one torch; the bridge holds at most two at a time, anyone crossing needs the torch, and a pair moves at the slower person's pace. Their times are 1, 2, 7, and 10 minutes. What is the least total time for all four to cross?
puzzle.approach: The two slowest should travel together - the trick is choosing who carries the torch back.
puzzle.answer: 17 minutes. 1&2 cross (2), 1 returns (1), 7&10 cross (10), 2 returns (2), 1&2 cross (2) = 17. Sending the two slowest together overlaps their times; using the two fastest as torch-bearers is optimal.

word_puzzle.title: Mixed Company
word_puzzle.body: Sort 16 words into four groups of four: TANGO, SAMBA, RUMBA, MAMBO, SALSA, TACO, TAMALE, NACHO, POKER, BRIDGE, RUMMY, HEARTS, SPOT, MOON, HIGH, SUN. One word (SALSA) is a trap that fits two themes.
word_puzzle.approach: Two groups share a tempting word - a dish and a dance both fit, but only one grouping leaves every set with four members.
word_puzzle.answer: Latin dances: TANGO, SAMBA, RUMBA, MAMBO. Mexican dishes: SALSA, TACO, TAMALE, NACHO. Card games: POKER, BRIDGE, RUMMY, HEARTS. ___+LIGHT: SPOT, MOON, HIGH, SUN. SALSA is the trap (dance vs dish); the dance slots are full, so it joins the dishes.
